title: Check an error
summary: Pass a function to toThrow so Jest can call it and catch the error.
introduction: Pass a function to toThrow so Jest can call it and catch the error. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Pass a function to toThrow so Jest can call it and catch the error.

blocks.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("rejects bad age", () => { const reject = () => { throw new Error("Bad age"); }; expect(reject).toThrow("Bad age"); });
blocks.title: Check an error

blocks.text: The test passes when the function throws an error with the expected message.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Change the message to see a useful failure.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not call the throwing function before passing it to expect.
For more detail later, use this [Jest further reading](https://jestjs.io/docs/getting-started).
